description: Epic status revival — done epics wake to running on open-issue link (single + batch), closed epics reject all links, MarkDone/auto-done stays rejected while open linked issues exist, so epic status always mirrors the reality of its child issues.

tasks.title: Single-link wake: done epic → running on open-issue link, closed rejects single link
tasks.spec: specs/epic-status-revival/spec.md#Done epic SHALL wake to running when an open issue is linked; specs/epic-status-revival/spec.md#Closed epic SHALL reject all issue links; specs/epic-status-revival/spec.md#Wake-up SHALL re-establish active-membership rows atomically with the link; specs/epic-status-revival/spec.md#Wake-up SHALL hand the newly linked open issue to autopilot
tasks.description: Add the `WakeFromDone` (done→running) domain transition and the `EpicClosedCannotLinkException` type plus the closed-guard inside `Epic.LinkIssue`. Restructure grain `LinkIssueAsync` from the binary `targetIsTerminal` gate into a three-way branch keyed on live epic status: closed → propagate the domain rejection; done → record link, classify the linked issue via a new `IsIssueOpenAsync` helper, wake to running + insert the `EpicActiveIssues` row + hoist the cross-aggregate ownership check before the wake, all in one `SaveChangesAsync`; non-terminal → unchanged. After a successful wake commit, tail-call the existing `TryStartNextAsync` so autopilot starts the new open issue with no caller-issued start. Map `EpicClosedCannotLinkException` to `409 EPIC_CLOSED_CANNOT_LINK` in the single-link `EpicRoutes` handler. Remove the archive-link comment at `EpicGrain.cs:80-82`. Add epic spec scenarios covering all single-link behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Linking an open issue to a done epic via `LinkIssueAsync` transitions the epic to `running`, persisted in the same `SaveChangesAsync` commit as the link row (spec: 'Done epic linked with an open issue transitions to running').
Linking an already-terminal issue to a done epic leaves the epic `done` with no wake and no active-membership row (spec: 'Done epic linked with an already-terminal issue stays done').
Wake reaches `running` without any caller `start`/`resume` and does not pass through `idle` (spec: 'Wake to running requires no manual start or resume').
Re-linking an issue already linked to a done epic is idempotent: no duplicate link row and no status change (spec: 'Idempotent re-link ... does not wake the epic').

A `closed` epic rejects a single link with `EpicClosedCannotLinkException`; the API returns `409 Conflict` with code `EPIC_CLOSED_CANNOT_LINK`, and no link/active-membership row is created (spec: 'Single link to a closed epic is rejected').

On wake, an `EpicActiveIssues` row for the newly linked open issue exists after commit, created in the same transaction as the status and link-row change (spec: 'Active-membership row added in the same commit as the wake-up').

If the linked open issue is already actively owned by another non-terminal epic, the link is rejected as a membership conflict, no second active row is created, and the done epic stays `done` (spec: 'Wake-up respects cross-aggregate active-membership uniqueness').

If the wake's `SaveChangesAsync` fails, the epic remains `done`, no active-membership/link row is left behind, and retrying the link performs the full wake again (spec: 'Wake-up that fails to persist rolls back the status change').

After wake, with no other in-progress linked issue, autopilot selects and starts the newly linked open issue with no caller-issued start (spec: 'Autopilot advances the newly linked open issue after wake-up').

New spec scenarios in `packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.Tests/Specs/Epic/` (e.g. `EpicLifecycleSpecs.cs` / `EpicMembershipSpecs.cs`) pass under SQLite with injected `TimeProvider` and fake `IIssueGrain` grains, no real DB/network, completing < 500ms each.
`dotnet build Mohist.sln` succeeds with warnings-as-errors and `npm test` (server) passes.
tasks.output: Updated `Epic.Transitions.cs` (WakeFromDone), `EpicLifecycleExceptions.cs` (EpicClosedCannotLinkException), `Epic.cs`/`LinkIssue` (closed guard), `EpicGrain.cs` (`LinkIssueAsync` three-way branch + `IsIssueOpenAsync` + ownership-check hoist + autopilot tail-call), `EpicRoutes.cs` (single-link 409 mapping), and new spec scenarios in `packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.Tests/Specs/Epic/`.
tasks.notes: Follow design decisions D1 (WakeFromDone transition, separate from LinkIssue, targets running not idle, emits EpicStatusChanged done→running), D2 (grain orchestrates wake in one commit; hoist GetActiveMembershipOwnerAsync before wake; reuse TryStartNextAsync at L643-680; preserve DbUpdateException catch at L123-132 for racing claims), D3 single-link half (EpicClosedCannotLinkException : InvalidOperationException carrying EpicId; closed guard before duplicate check in LinkIssue; 409 EPIC_CLOSED_CANNOT_LINK alongside DUPLICATE_EPIC_MEMBERSHIP). Do NOT add a dedicated EpicWoken event (D1 rejection + D6). The five-state enum, autopilot internals, auto-done trigger, unlink, and Reopen are untouched.

tasks.title: Batch-link wake: done epic wakes on batch with open issue, closed rejects whole batch
tasks.spec: specs/epic-status-revival/spec.md#Batch link SHALL apply the same wake-up rules as single link; specs/epic-status-revival/spec.md#Closed epic SHALL reject all issue links
tasks.description: Restructure grain `LinkIssuesAsync` (batch) symmetrically to single link: reject a `closed` target once before the loop by throwing `EpicClosedCannotLinkException` (no per-item outcomes), and replace the single `targetIsTerminal` snapshot with a per-item decision based on the live in-memory `row.Status` (refreshed by `MapToRow` after each commit). For each item: if `row.Status == done` and the item is open → wake in that item's commit (flips in-memory status to `running` so later items take the normal non-terminal path); if only-terminal items are linked, status stays `done` for the whole batch. The first open link wakes exactly once; subsequent open links are plain non-terminal links. Reuse T-001's `WakeFromDone`, `IsIssueOpenAsync`, ownership check, and active-row insert per item. Invoke `TryStartNextAsync` once after the loop if the epic ended up `running` and was `done` at entry. Map `EpicClosedCannotLinkException` to `409 EPIC_CLOSED_CANNOT_LINK` in the batch-link `EpicRoutes` handler. Add batch spec scenarios.
acceptanceCriteria: A batch link to a `done` epic containing at least one open issue that is successfully linked wakes the epic to `running`, atomically with the successful link(s) (spec: 'Batch containing at least one open issue wakes a done epic to running').
A batch link to a `done` epic containing only already-terminal issues leaves the epic `done` with no wake (spec: 'Batch containing only terminal issues leaves a done epic done').

A batch link to a `closed` epic is rejected as a whole with `409 Conflict` (code `EPIC_CLOSED_CANNOT_LINK`); no per-item linked/conflict outcomes are produced and no link rows are created (spec: 'Batch link to a closed epic is rejected as a whole').
Within one batch, wake fires at most once (on the first open link); subsequent open links in the same batch do not re-invoke `WakeFromDone` and do not throw (gated on live `row.Status == done`).

Per-item persistence semantics are preserved: a single item failure does not roll back earlier successful links in the batch, and a partially-woken epic correctly ends up `running` with open work (matches design risk note on batch partial wake).
After a batch that woke the epic, autopilot picks up the newly linked open issue with no caller-issued start.

New batch spec scenarios in `packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.Tests/Specs/Epic/` (e.g. `EpicBatchMembershipSpecs.cs` / `EpicBatchMembershipApiSpecs.cs`) pass under SQLite with injected `TimeProvider` and fake grains, no real DB/network, < 500ms each.
`dotnet build Mohist.sln` succeeds with warnings-as-errors and `npm test` (server) passes.
tasks.output: Updated `EpicGrain.cs` (`LinkIssuesAsync` closed pre-check + per-item live-status wake) and `EpicRoutes.cs` (batch-link 409 mapping), plus new batch spec scenarios in `packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.Tests/Specs/Epic/`.
tasks.notes: Follow design D4 (per-item decision from live row.Status refreshed by MapToRow; wake-once on first open link; TryStartNextAsync once after loop if epic ended running and was done at entry) and D3 batch half (closed checked once before the loop, throws EpicClosedCannotLinkException, no per-item outcomes). Reuse all domain primitives (WakeFromDone, EpicClosedCannotLinkException, IsIssueOpenAsync) from T-001 — do not re-add them. Do NOT pre-classify the whole batch or wake before any durable commit (rejected alternative in D4).

tasks.title: Pin invariant 2: regression tests for MarkDone / auto-done rejection while open linked issues exist
tasks.spec: specs/epic-status-revival/spec.md#MarkDone and auto-done SHALL be rejected while open linked issues exist
tasks.description: Invariant 2 — `MarkDone`/auto-done rejected while any open linked issue exists — is already implemented (`Epic.MarkDone` throws `EpicNotReadyToMarkDoneException` when openLinkedNumbers.Count > 0; `TryAutoMarkDoneAsync` and `ReconcileAfterTerminalInternalAsync` are no-ops when open issues remain). Add regression spec scenarios to freeze this as the symmetric pin to wake-up, closing the status-mirrors-reality loop (open issues exhausted → auto-done; new open issue linked → wake). No production code change.
acceptanceCriteria: A spec scenario asserts that `MarkDone` (via `SetStatusAsync("done")`) on an epic with at least one open linked issue raises `EpicNotReadyToMarkDoneException` and leaves the status unchanged (spec: 'Manual mark done with an open linked issue is rejected').

A spec scenario asserts that `AutoMarkDoneIfReadyAsync` (and the reconcile-on-terminal-event path) on an epic with at least one open linked issue is a no-op that leaves the status non-terminal (spec: 'Auto-done with an open linked issue is a no-op').

New scenarios live in `packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.Tests/Specs/Epic/` (e.g. `EpicAutoDoneSpecs.cs` / `EpicLifecycleSpecs.cs`), run under SQLite with injected `TimeProvider` and fake grains, no real DB/network, and complete < 500ms each.
Scenarios pass against the current codebase with zero production change, confirming invariant 2 holds as the symmetric close of the wake-up loop.
`npm test` (server) passes.
tasks.output: New regression spec scenarios in `packages/server/tests/Mohist.Server.Tests/Specs/Epic/` (e.g. `EpicAutoDoneSpecs.cs` / `EpicLifecycleSpecs.cs`) pinning MarkDone and auto-done rejection while open linked issues exist.
tasks.notes: Per design D5, this is a pure test-add task — no production change. Prefer `EpicAutoDoneSpecs.cs` for the auto-done no-op scenario to minimize file overlap with T-001's single-link wake scenarios. Independent of T-001/T-002: invariant 2 is already implemented and this task consumes none of their output, so it may execute in parallel with T-001.
